items.title: Genome profiling and HiFi assembly
items.summary: Estimate genome size and heterozygosity from k-mers, assemble primary and alternate contigs from the HiFi reads of a green alga, and check both assemblies with read k-mers and conserved genes.
items.task_text:
Genome profiling and HiFi assembly

Task
Characterize the supplied Picochlorum BPE23 HiFi library, construct primary and alternate assemblies, and assess their sequence, graph, k-mer and conserved-ortholog evidence. Explain contiguity, redundancy and completeness without calling internal consistency independent biological validation. Use k-mer multiplicity to model genome size and heterozygosity, and resolve high-accuracy long-read overlaps into primary and alternate assembly graphs. Assess allelic redundancy as well as contiguity. Use read k-mers and conserved orthologs as complementary evidence, distinguishing sequence accuracy from genome completeness.

Inputs
- One complete HiFi read library and its file/identity manifest.
- chlorophyta_odb10 ortholog resources from snapshot all-odb10-2026-03-19-213122.
- The two residual-adapter definitions in adapters.fasta (protocol constants, supplied with the input manifest).
- output-layouts.json lists required statistic labels only; it contains no measurements.

Key parameters and conditions
- Use k=21 and fit a diploid four-component negative-binomial mixture to the k-mer multiplicity histogram, estimating heterozygous/homozygous and repeat contributions. Estimate coverage from the data without a maximum-coverage cutoff. The histogram and k-mer validation use the complete original library.
- For assembly, discard an entire read if either supplied adapter matches anywhere in either orientation, with at least 35 nt overlap and error rate at most 0.10, allowing indels. Do not retain a trimmed remainder or add quality trimming. Retain the adapter-free reads and rejection counts.
- Assemble using only the supplied HiFi reads with haplotype-aware error correction and phased overlap graphs, incorporating allelic-redundancy removal within assembly. Produce primary contigs plus alternate contigs, not a claim of two fully phased chromosomes; use the fitted homozygous coverage and genome-size estimates. Assess both assemblies by spliced protein-to-genome alignment with minimizer seeding, chaining and frameshift handling against the supplied lineage proteins. Distinguish single-copy, duplicated, fragmented and missing orthologs, and separately report genes whose complementary portions align at two positions.
- Retain primary and alternate results, missing-ortholog records and zero-error QV values. No between-library comparison is required.
- Perform three rounds of haplotype-aware read correction. Remove contained and other redundant haplotigs using the most aggressive purge regime, with a read-level similarity threshold of 0.55; do not disable allelic-redundancy removal.
- Use canonical 21-mers without a multiplicity cap. Set the homozygous assembly coverage to floor(2 × the fitted per-copy coverage); use the upper fitted haploid-length bound as the expected genome size. Retained assembly reads must have at least one base. GFA segments must contain their nucleotide sequences, not only length placeholders.

Required results
1. final_answer/01_read_qc/
   FASTQ + JSON + TSV
   Retained reads in retained.fastq.gz; adapter-rejection counts in adapter_rejection.json (read_counts and basepair_counts); input_statistics.tsv is a two-column metric/value table of the complete input read statistics with the input_statistics metric labels in output-layouts.json, where average per-base quality is the Phred-scaled mean per-base error probability over all bases rather than the mean of quality scores. Counts are not optional plots. Files: adapter_rejection.json, input_statistics.tsv, retained.fastq.gz.
2. final_answer/02_kmer_histogram.tsv
   TSV
   Headerless two columns: multiplicity, count; the full histogram.
3. final_answer/03_genome_profile/
   native text reports
   model_parameters.txt: the six fitted point estimates as one tab-separated record, in order: repetitiveness (duplication) parameter, heterozygosity rate, per-copy k-mer coverage, overdispersion (bias) parameter, haploid length implied by the non-error k-mers at the fitted coverage, and model topology (0 for this diploid model); summary.txt: lower and upper bounds for homozygosity, heterozygosity, haploid/repeat/unique length, model fit and read error. Diagnostic plots may accompany the reports. Files: model_parameters.txt, summary.txt.
4. final_answer/04_assembly_graphs/
   GFA
   Raw and processed unitig graphs and primary/alternate contig graphs, each labeled. Files: alternate_contig_graph.gfa, primary_contig_graph.gfa, processed_unitigs.gfa, raw_unitigs.gfa.
5. final_answer/05_assemblies/
   FASTA
   primary.fasta and alternate.fasta, including every retained contig. Files: alternate.fasta, primary.fasta.
6. final_answer/06_assembly_statistics/
   TSV
   For each assembly, a complete metric/value statistics table and a two-column contig/length table. Include the expected genome size and its length-dependent contiguity statistics; do not substitute a FASTA index. Use the assembly_statistics metric labels in output-layouts.json. Files: alternate.lengths.tsv, alternate.statistics.tsv, primary.lengths.tsv, primary.statistics.tsv.
7. final_answer/07_kmer_validation/
   standard k-mer report tables
   Complete copy-number and assembly spectra, auxiliary histograms, global and per-contig QV and completeness reports for primary and alternate assemblies. Preserve report content and contig identifiers. Files: alternate.only.tsv, alternate.qv.tsv, alternate.spectra-cn.tsv, completeness.tsv, dist_only.tsv, global.qv.tsv, only.tsv, primary.only.tsv, primary.qv.tsv, primary.spectra-cn.tsv, spectra-asm.tsv, spectra-cn.tsv.
8. final_answer/08_ortholog_validation/
   native ortholog tables + FASTA
   Complete ortholog tables and translated proteins for both assemblies, with missing calls retained. Files: alternate.full_table.tsv, alternate.proteins.fasta, primary.full_table.tsv, primary.proteins.fasta.

items.title: ATAC-seq peaks and normalized signal
items.summary: Trim, align, filter and deduplicate two mouse ATAC-seq libraries, call peaks and summits, and build two differently normalized signal tracks per library.
items.task_text:
ATAC-seq peaks and normalized signal

Task
Analyze the two mouse paired-end ATAC-seq libraries separately on mm10. Produce accessible-region evidence and two explicitly defined normalized signal profiles per library. Treat accessibility as local narrow enrichment in reference-aligned reads without an external control. Use summit-centered windows to define the accessible-region union, and compare total-library versus accessible-region normalization of the same shifted/extended signal. Keep the alignment-record and paired-fragment units distinct.

Inputs
- Two complete paired-read libraries with sample/mate identities.
- mm10 reference and chromosome lengths.

Key parameters and conditions
- Use Q30 as the qualified-base threshold and allow at most 70% unqualified bases. Preserve library and mate identities. Keep paired reads with at most five ambiguous bases per mate and length at least 15 nt after overlap-based adapter removal; do not merge mates or add fixed/sliding-window trimming.
- Use an FM-index multiseed, gapped end-to-end paired alignment method with a very-sensitive search, inward-facing orientation, insert range 0–1,000 bp and dovetail pairs allowed. Apply MAPQ≥30 to each alignment record independently and require its proper-pair flag; do not add a requirement that both mates pass MAPQ together. Exclude mitochondrial alignments, then remove duplicates. Report chromosome statistics, duplicate metrics and insert-size distribution through 500 bp. Identify coordinate duplicates by aligned template coordinates, retaining the representative with the greatest sum of base qualities.
- For no-control narrow peaks and signal, use a per-alignment BED representation, effective genome size 2,308,840,607, shift −100, extension 200 and q<0.05; retain all records reaching peak calling. Expand each one-base summit by 500 bp on each side, clip to chromosome bounds and merge overlapping or book-ended windows within each library.
- Count all post-deduplication alignment records and records whose reference spans overlap the merged window union. Count each record at most once; do not substitute fragment counts or aligned-block overlap.
- From the shifted/extended treatment pileup from Poisson-background narrow-enrichment calling, produce 50-bp bins of mean per-base signal, treating uncovered bases as zero; use only in-genome bases for a shortened terminal bin. Scale by 10^6 divided by either the total retained-record count or the union-overlapping count. A zero denominator makes that profile undefined: retain the zero count and report it, rather than fabricate a zero profile. These are not bin sums or unextended-read coverage tracks.
- Call sub-peak summits, retaining distinct summits sharing an interval. Report chromosome counts on the unfiltered alignment and insert lengths on deduplicated read pairs (one observation per pair). Use the complete supplied chromosome dictionary and coordinate-sorted BAMs. Signal bins begin at the first genomic base.

Required results
1. final_answer/01_read_processing/{sample}/
   FASTQ + JSON
   Processed mate files and the complete native JSON quality/processing report. Files: {sample}/forward.fastq.gz, {sample}/qc.json, {sample}/reverse.fastq.gz.
2. final_answer/02_alignment_stages/{sample}/
   BAM + native text/TSV reports
   Aligned, selected and deduplicated BAMs; alignment summary, chromosome idxstats, coordinate-duplicate library metrics and a headerless two-column insert-length/frequency histogram through 500 bp. Files: {sample}/aligned.bam, {sample}/deduplicated.bam, {sample}/duplicates.txt, {sample}/filtered.bam, {sample}/idxstats.tsv, {sample}/insert_lengths.tsv, {sample}/mapping.txt.
3. final_answer/03_peaks/{sample}/
   narrowPeak + BED + TSV
   Ten-column narrowPeak, one-base summit BED and the complete peak-calling TSV report; retain sub-peak summits. Files: {sample}/peaks.narrowPeak, {sample}/report.tsv, {sample}/summits.bed.
4. final_answer/04_peak_windows/{sample}/
   TSV + BED
   Headerless windows.tsv: chromosome, start, end, summit label, score; union.bed: chromosome, start, end. Coordinates are zero-based half-open. Files: {sample}/union.bed, {sample}/windows.tsv.
5. final_answer/05_signal_scaling/{sample}/
   text
   One number in each of all_count.txt, union_count.txt, all_factor.txt and union_factor.txt. Files: {sample}/all_count.txt, {sample}/all_factor.txt, {sample}/union_count.txt, {sample}/union_factor.txt.
6. final_answer/06_raw_pileup/{sample}.bedgraph
   bedGraph
   Unscaled shifted/extended treatment pileup.
7. final_answer/07_signal_total/{sample}.bw
   bigWig
   50-bp profile scaled by the total retained-record count.
8. final_answer/08_signal_in_union/{sample}.bw
   bigWig
   50-bp profile scaled by the union-overlapping record count.

items.title: 16S amplicon sequence variants and taxonomy
items.summary: Infer exact sequence variants in 24 environmental 16S V4 libraries, remove chimeras across samples and assign taxonomy.
items.task_text:
Amplicon sequence variants and taxonomy

Task
Reconstruct sequence variants and taxonomic assignments for all 24 environmental 16S V4 libraries, preserving sample identities and uncertainty. Infer exact amplicon sequence variants with a quality-dependent sequencing-error model rather than fixed-similarity OTU clustering. Reconstruct paired sequences from their overlap and assess chimeras across samples. Assign taxonomy using a reference-trained sequence classifier with bootstrap support.

Inputs
- Twenty-four paired 2×250 MiSeq 515F/806R libraries and their sample/mate manifest; library-name prefixes are not verified run labels.
- Supplied 515F/806R primer definitions: primers.tsv.
- SILVA 132 taxonomy resources.

Key parameters and conditions
- Remove fixed leading prefixes equal to the lengths of the supplied forward 515F and reverse 806R primers. The truncation positions in the original reads are 199 forward and 200 reverse, before removing those prefixes. This is fixed positional trimming, not primer-match filtering. Discard a read pair if either trimmed mate is shorter than its required post-trimming length. Allow at most two expected errors per mate, no ambiguous bases, quality truncation at 2 and PhiX removal.
- Infer sequence variants by testing abundance against a quality-dependent substitution-error model learned with LOESS and self-consistent sequence inference. Learn directional errors separately for each library and do not pool libraries for inference. Require at least 12 bp of exact paired overlap rather than concatenation. Error learning uses input order, a 10^8-base learning target (or all available bases when fewer), at most ten self-consistency iterations and OMEGA_C=0; this learning target does not subsample the reads submitted for denoising.
- Combine all samples before consensus chimera removal. Do not rarefy, drop samples or apply another ASV abundance/length filter. Use taxonomy bootstrap threshold 50 and seed 0; retain unclassified ranks and confidence evidence. Use reference-trained k-mer naive-Bayes taxonomy assignment on the supplied orientation, without reverse-complement searching or an additional exact species-match stage.

Required results
1. final_answer/01_quality/{sample}/
   native quality reports + plots
   Input quality profiles and filtering/retention reports for both mates.
2. final_answer/02_filtered_reads/{sample}/
   FASTQ
   Both complete filtered mate files. Files: {sample}/forward.fastq.gz, {sample}/reverse.fastq.gz.
3. final_answer/03_error_models/{sample}/
   RDS
   Forward/reverse learned error models and numeric error estimates. Files: {sample}/forward.rds, {sample}/reverse.rds.
4. final_answer/04_denoising/{sample}/
   RDS
   Directional sequence inference and abundance evidence. Files: {sample}/forward.rds, {sample}/reverse.rds.
5. final_answer/05_pair_merges/{sample}/
   RDS
   merged.rds: the accepted paired-merge data frame, including sequence, abundance, forward/reverse inference-row references, nmatch, nmismatch, nindel, prefer and accept. Failed overlaps are represented by losses in read tracking, not fabricated merge rows. Files: {sample}/merged.rds.
6. final_answer/06_asv_counts_unfiltered/
   TSV
   counts.tsv: one row per exact ASV sequence, first column sequence, then S01–S24 integer count columns; retain zero counts and all sample columns. Files: counts.tsv.
7. final_answer/07_asv_counts_nonchimeric/
   TSV
   counts.tsv: one row per exact ASV sequence, first column sequence, then S01–S24 integer count columns; retain zero counts and all sample columns. Files: counts.tsv.
8. final_answer/08_taxonomy/
   TSV
   taxonomy.tsv and bootstrap.tsv: sequence followed by Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus. Use NA for unclassified/missing values; bootstrap values are percentages. Files: bootstrap.tsv, taxonomy.tsv.
9. final_answer/09_read_tracking/
   TSV
   counts.tsv columns: sample, input_pairs, filtered_pairs, denoised_forward, denoised_reverse, merged_pairs, pre_chimera, nonchimeric. Explain major losses briefly in method.md. Files: counts.tsv.

items.title: Paired RNA-seq effects and donor robustness
items.summary: Align eight human RNA-seq libraries from four donors, test treatment effects with donor pairing, repeat the test leaving out each donor, run GO enrichment with gene-length correction, and assemble transcripts.
items.task_text:
Paired RNA-seq effects and donor robustness

Task
Estimate treatment effects and donor sensitivity in eight paired-end human RNA-seq libraries, together with condition-blind transcript-structure evidence. Model gene-level counts with a negative-binomial generalized linear model that accounts for donor pairing. Examine whether treatment effects persist when each donor pair is omitted, and account for gene-length selection bias in functional enrichment. Use annotation-unguided, genome-aligned transcript assembly for structural evidence, not as independent validation of expression effects.

Inputs
- Eight libraries with 2,000,000 read pairs each; hg38 and GENCODE 47 annotation; the supplied human Ensembl gene-to-GO Biological Process mapping snapshot identified in the input manifest.
- Controls S01/S03/S05/S07; treated S02/S04/S06/S08. Donors: D01=S03/S04, D02=S07/S08, D03=S05/S06, D04=S01/S02.

Key parameters and conditions
- Use maximal-mappable-seed stitching for splice-aware alignment and overlap assignment to gene-level exon unions. Do not trim or subsample further. Preserve splice-strand evidence and use the same alignments for assembly and counting. Count unstranded fragments over annotated gene-exon unions with at least one overlapping base. Exclude multi-mapping fragments and fragments ambiguously assigned to multiple genes; use integer counts, with no fractional allocation or largest-overlap assignment. Exclude chimeric fragments, retain duplicates and add no MAPQ/region filter. Retain counts, assignment summaries and native gene lengths.
- Use a negative-binomial GLM with gene-wise dispersions moderated toward a fitted mean–dispersion trend and median-of-ratios normalization. Define E by count≥10 in at least four original libraries and keep E fixed. Use a donor-adjusted treatment design (~donor+treatment): all libraries (F0), then omit each complete pair (LO_D01–LO_D04). Use ratio size factors, parametric dispersion, Wald tests and BH adjustment; unshrunken effects, Cook's filtering, no outlier replacement or independent filtering. Positive log2 effects are treated/control; retain non-estimable values.
- Select up/down lists separately using gene-level BH-adjusted p<0.05 and |log2 effect|≥1, with direction determined by sign. Use exon-union lengths and Wallenius correction for Biological Process enrichment. The supplied mapping includes ancestor-propagated BP membership and the literal Other bin for genes lacking that membership; retain this bin in the full tested/BH family, but do not interpret it as a GO term. Keep unannotated genes in the background. Significant GO terms have GO-level adjusted p<0.05. Category size 10–500 defines an interpretation stratum, not a smaller correction family.
- The full-fit background requires positive length and finite effect/p/adjusted-p in F0; the shared background requires these in all five fits. Run both directions for F0 on the full background and for all five fits on the shared background. Preserve all categories, PWFs and mappings. Strip only numeric gene-ID versions at this interface and retain the crosswalk.
- Use splice-graph transcript reconstruction with network-flow abundance estimation: assemble each library separately, then merge the reconstructed transcript models across all eight libraries without condition selection. Assemble each library without an annotation guide, keeping transcripts of at least 200 nt; require coverage of at least 10 for multi-exon and 4.75 for single-exon transcripts, junction coverage of at least 10 with at least 10 anchoring bases on each side, isoform fraction 0.01 and locus gap 50. For the merge use gap 0, minimum length 50, coverage 0, FPKM/TPM 1 and isoform fraction 0.01, keeping no retained introns. Same-read structural evidence is not independent biological validation.
- For spliced alignment use splice-junction-based filtering, at most 20 mapping loci, minimum splice overhang 8 (1 at annotated junctions), at most 4% mismatches relative to the read-pair length with no separate absolute mismatch cap, alignment score and matched bases each at least 66% of the read-pair length, intron length 20–1,000,000 and paired-read gap at most 1,000,000. Use the supplied annotation for junction indexing with overhang 100. The fixed E domain is used for size factors, dispersion fitting, testing and gene-level BH adjustment.

Required results
1. final_answer/01_alignments/{sample}/
   BAM + index + native reports
   Eight splice-aware alignments and mapping/strand evidence. Files: {sample}/aligned.bam, {sample}/mapping.txt.
2. final_answer/02_gene_counts/{sample}/
   native count tables
   Complete counts, assignment summaries and exon-union gene lengths. Use gene_id/count, status/count and gene_id/length tables with headers. Files: {sample}/assignment.tsv, {sample}/counts.tsv, {sample}/lengths.tsv.
3. final_answer/03_fixed_gene_domain/
   TSV
   matrix.tsv and eligible.tsv have gene_id, S01–S08 and eligible (0/1); the former contains the full counted domain and the latter E. Preserve original/version-stripped identifiers in the crosswalk. Files: eligible.tsv, matrix.tsv.
4. final_answer/04_differential_expression/{fit}/
   TSV
   results.tsv columns: gene_id, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj. Keep all E rows and NA. Fit directory names are F0 and LO_D01–LO_D04. Files: {fit}/results.tsv.
5. final_answer/05_normalization/{fit}/
   TSV
   counts.tsv: gene_id and every included sample; size_factors.tsv: sample, size_factor. Files: {fit}/counts.tsv, {fit}/size_factors.tsv.
6. final_answer/06_go_full/{direction}/
   TSV
   universe.tsv: gene_id, length, pwf, selected (0/1); membership.tsv: gene_id, category, one row per link; categories.tsv: category, over_represented_pvalue, under_represented_pvalue, numDEInCat, numInCat, term, ontology, p_adjust_over_represented, p_adjust_under_represented. Retain the complete tested family, including Other, and both adjustment directions. Files: down/categories.tsv, down/membership.tsv, down/universe.tsv, up/categories.tsv, up/membership.tsv, up/universe.tsv.
7. final_answer/07_go_robustness/{fit}/{direction}/
   TSV
   universe.tsv: gene_id, length, pwf, selected (0/1); membership.tsv: gene_id, category, one row per link; categories.tsv: category, over_represented_pvalue, under_represented_pvalue, numDEInCat, numInCat, term, ontology, p_adjust_over_represented, p_adjust_under_represented. Retain the complete tested family, including Other, and both adjustment directions. Files: {fit}/down/categories.tsv, {fit}/down/membership.tsv, {fit}/down/universe.tsv, {fit}/up/categories.tsv, {fit}/up/membership.tsv, {fit}/up/universe.tsv.
8. final_answer/08_library_assemblies/{sample}.gtf
   GTF
   All eight condition-blind per-library transcript assemblies.
9. final_answer/09_common_assembly.gtf
   GTF
   Combined assembly from all eight libraries.
10. final_answer/10_splice_junctions/{sample}/
   native junction tables
   All per-library splice-junction tables, retaining strand and support fields. Files: {sample}/junctions.tsv.
11. final_answer/11_robustness_interpretation.md
   Markdown + references to named results
   A concise comparison of treatment-effect and GO sensitivity across fits; distinguish legitimate empty selections from failed fits.

items.title: Single-cell populations and marker genes
items.summary: Filter, normalize and cluster a single-cell count matrix with the stated settings, and test marker genes for every cluster.
items.task_text:
Single-cell populations and marker evidence

Task
Identify cell populations and their positive-expression markers from the supplied count matrix. Cell-type annotation is not requested. Identify populations through variable-gene expression structure after nuisance adjustment: use a low-dimensional expression representation and local-neighbor graph communities, not supervised cell-type labels. Assess population markers against the remaining cells using the full retained gene domain.

Inputs
- The complete single-cell count matrix, cell identifiers and gene identifiers/symbols.

Key parameters and conditions
- Retain genes detected in at least three input cells, then cells with 200–6,000 detected genes inclusive and mitochondrial percentage<15% using MT- symbols. QC uses the retained full-gene domain before variable-gene selection.
- Normalize library size to 10,000 and use natural-log(1+x). Select variable genes by dispersion standardized within mean-expression bins: 20 bins, 0.0125<log(1+mean)<3 and normalized dispersion>0.5.
- Regress total counts and mitochondrial percentage; center the selected genes, scale residuals to unit sample variance and clip at ±10. Use the first ten centered, unwhitened PCs, Euclidean distance and neighborhoods of 15 cells including self, with seed 0. Retain locally scaled fuzzy-simplicial-set union connectivity weights as graph evidence. For clustering, use the unweighted, undirected union of its nonzero edges without self-edges, with Louvain, the Reichardt–Bornholdt configuration-model objective, resolution 1.0 and seed 0. A two-dimensional embedding is not a substitute for the PCA coordinates or graph.
- For each population, apply a two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test without tie correction to full-domain log-normalized expression, against all other retained cells. Apply BH within each population across the full retained gene domain. Define the effect as the following log-scale-mean effect: log2((expm1(mean log-normalized expression in the population)+10^-9)/(expm1(mean log-normalized expression in the rest)+10^-9)), not a ratio of arithmetic mean raw counts. Positive markers require effect>0 and adjusted p<0.05; retain nonsignificant genes and all test results.
- Gene identities are the supplied gene symbols made unique in input order. For dispersion selection, recover linear expression with expm1, compute log(variance/mean), bin log1p(mean) into 20 equal-width bins and standardize dispersion within each bin. Report the standardized Wilcoxon z statistic, not the raw rank-sum U statistic.
- Each H5AD uses observation names for cells and variable names for genes. A stage expression matrix is stored in X, not only in an unnamed layer. Keep the complete marker-test gene domain in raw/X with raw/var identities. The clustering column is obs/louvain.

   Filtered gene domain, full count matrix and detection evidence. Stored fields: var/n_cells. Files: counts.h5ad.

items.title: Replicate-supported CUT&RUN consensus
items.summary: Call peaks in two CUT&RUN libraries and in their depth-balanced pool, keep the pooled peaks whose summits both libraries support, and build signal tracks.
items.task_text:
Replicate-supported CUT&RUN consensus

Task
Construct a replicate-supported CUT&RUN consensus from two paired-end human libraries, preserving the evidence for both accepted and unsupported candidates. Use depth-balanced pooled reads to nominate narrow enrichment candidates, and require summit support from both individual libraries. Preserve the distinction between candidate discovery, replicate support and signal averaging; a simple union of the individual peak lists is not the requested consensus.

Inputs
- Paired-end S01 and S02 libraries, hg19 reference/chromosome lengths and supplied adapters; no control library.

Key parameters and conditions
- Use error-tolerant 3′ adapter alignment to the supplied sequences with minimum overlap 3 nt, error rate 0.10 and indels allowed; trim 3′ low-quality ends at Q30, not 5′ ends. Discard a pair if either mate is shorter than 15 nt. Use an FM-index multiseed, gapped end-to-end paired alignment method with a very-sensitive search, inward-facing orientation, insert range 0–1,000 bp and dovetail allowed. Select each record by proper-pair flag and MAPQ≥30; do not add a requirement that both mates pass MAPQ together. Remove coordinate duplicates by aligned template coordinates with the highest base-quality-sum representative. Do not add mitochondrial, blacklist or other regional exclusions.
- Call narrow peaks for each library from its complete deduplicated alignments (before depth balancing) and for the balanced pool, using per-alignment BED, genome size 2.7e9, q≤0.05, shift −100, extension 200 and no additional peak-caller duplicate removal. Retain distinct summits sharing an interval.
- Balance library depth by template-name-hashed proportional selection of SAM/BAM alignment records (subsample / subsample-seed, seed 1), retaining or discarding all records of a template together. Set the retention fraction from the smaller retained-alignment count divided by the current library count; report the target and realized counts. This is reproducible proportional sampling, not exact-count reservoir sampling, truncation or signal normalization.
- Partition the union of unpooled peak intervals into support segments, retaining segments covered by either one or both libraries; the qualifying segments are those supported by both. Relate every pooled candidate to every support segment it overlaps, one- or two-library alike, and keep one no-overlap row for a candidate that overlaps none. Accept a pooled candidate only when its summit lies in a qualifying segment, using zero-based half-open coordinates; its relation to that segment is its accepted relation.
- Deliver each library's shifted/extended treatment pileup per million retained alignment records and their equal-library mean in 50 bp bins, treating absent values as zero; do not substitute unshifted aligned-block coverage or the pooled signal.
- Use the complete supplied 93-sequence chromosome dictionary. The balance target and realized counts count retained alignment records, not templates.

Required results
1. final_answer/01_read_processing/{sample}/
   FASTQ + text
   Processed mate files and the complete native adapter/quality-trimming text report. Files: {sample}/forward.fastq.gz, {sample}/reverse.fastq.gz, {sample}/trimming.txt.
2. final_answer/02_alignment_stages/{sample}/
   BAM + index + native reports
   Coordinate-sorted alignment, selection and deduplication stages and their metrics; mapping.txt is the aligner's own paired-alignment summary (concordant, discordant and mate-level alignment counts). Files: {sample}/aligned.bam, {sample}/deduplicated.bam, {sample}/duplicates.txt, {sample}/filtered.bam, {sample}/mapping.txt.
3. final_answer/03_depth_balance/
   BAM + BED6 + text
   Each library’s balanced BAM, the corresponding BED6 used for joint calling, and realized record count; target.txt contains one integer. Preserve S01/S02 identities. Files: S01.bam, S01.bed, S01.count.txt, S02.bam, S02.bed, S02.count.txt, target.txt.
4. final_answer/04_peaks/{S01,S02,pool}/
   narrowPeak
   Complete ten-column unpooled and pooled peak candidates including summit offsets. Files: S01/peaks.narrowPeak, S02/peaks.narrowPeak, pool/peaks.narrowPeak.
5. final_answer/05_replicate_support/
   TSV

6. final_answer/06_candidate_relations/

items.summary: Identify peptides in one mass-spectrometry run of a microbial community and estimate how much labelled carbon each peptide took up.
items.task_text:
Carbon-isotope incorporation in a microbial metaproteome

Task
Identify peptides and quantify carbon-isotope incorporation from the supplied centroided liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry acquisition and metaproteome FASTA. This is one acquisition, not biological replication; do not infer differential abundance or organism-level activity. Use natural-abundance peptide isotope envelopes and chromatographic elution as MS1 feature anchors. Link them to database-supported MS/MS identifications, then infer carbon incorporation by sequence-informed isotope-pattern fitting and decomposition. Estimate a carbon-labeling distribution, not a fixed light/heavy amino-acid pair ratio.

Inputs
- One complete centroided liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry acquisition and its acquisition metadata.
- The metaproteome FASTA with protein accession identities.

Key parameters and conditions
- Detect MS1 anchors without prior peptide identifications using mass-shift isotope-pattern filtering and m/z–RT clustering, in an unlabelled singlet mode rather than fixed light/heavy pairs. Require charges 1–4, 3–6 isotope peaks, m/z tolerance 6 ppm and intensity at least 1,000. The isotope intensities must correlate with peptide averagine by both Pearson and Spearman at ≥0.4. Use a typical elution scale of 40 s for clustering, not a maximum duration; retain features lasting at least 2 s.
- Use spectral-generating-function database scoring, fully tryptic specificity allowing cleavage before proline, fixed cysteine carbamidomethylation and variable methionine oxidation (at most two variable modifications per peptide). Search lengths 6–40, isotope offsets 0/+1 and precursor tolerance 10 ppm. For spectra lacking charge information, consider charges 2–3; do not filter known charges by this range. Preserve all compatible protein accessions. Use the low-resolution instrument scoring model and the fragmentation method recorded in each spectrum. Do not impose a missed-cleavage-count cap. In both search-identification outputs, retain every hit tied for first rank within a spectrum, preserving their original order. Protein mapping distinguishes I from L, allows no residue mismatches and permits protein N-terminal methionine removal.
- Use a target-decoy database with peptide-internal pseudoreversal: tryptic cleavage sites (no cleavage before proline) and each peptide’s terminal residues are preserved; decoy accessions have prefix DECOY_. For PSM-level FDR, count one leading hit per spectrum; when first rank is tied, use the first hit in the original search-result order. At each score threshold, let D and T count decoy and target leading hits with scores at least as good as that threshold; a hit mapping to both target and decoy proteins counts as target. Estimate FDR as D/T, without a pseudocount, and obtain each target hit’s q-value as the minimum FDR over thresholds that include it. Pool charge states and accept target PSMs at q≤0.01. Retain all target leading-hit q-values and the accepted set; do not substitute peptide- or protein-level FDR.
- Map accepted identifications to features using 20 ppm m/z and 5 s RT tolerances with compatible charge. Use the same complete generated search database for identification and isotope inference. Only feature-linked identifications passing the PSM threshold enter incorporation inference; retain unassigned identifications separately in the mapping output. For matching, use feature centroid m/z and its chromatographic hull RT range expanded by 5 s; do not replace the RT range by a ±5 s window around its apex. Compare the calculated peptide-ion m/z with a ±20 ppm interval centered on the feature m/z.
- Estimate carbon labeling using m/z tolerance 10 ppm, RT tolerance 30 s and minimum MS1 intensity 10. Set isotope-pattern correlation and extracted-ion-chromatogram correlation thresholds to 0.7, and decomposition fit R² threshold to 0.7. Collect incorporation estimates at correlation maxima from sequence-informed isotope-pattern decomposition, without clustering by relative isotope abundance.
- Retain relative isotope abundance, labeling estimates, fit quality, ambiguity and group summaries. The peptide-level incorporation report must exclude purely natural-abundance peptides, while retaining unresolved fields actually reported within the included records.
- During protein mapping, allow at most three ambiguous amino-acid codes. In isotope inference combine decomposition weights within ±5 percentage points, require at least two consecutive isotopic intensities and at least half of the expected isotope peaks to be observed; retain 95% of the theoretical carbon-isotope pattern intensity.

Required results
1. final_answer/01_search_database.fasta
   FASTA
   Complete generated target/decoy search database, with construction recorded in method.md.
2. final_answer/02_features/
   featureXML
   All detected features with identities, coordinates, intensities and isotope-envelope evidence. Include the stored feature quality score and complete isotope hulls. Files: features.featureXML.
3. final_answer/03_identifications/
   idXML
   Both original search identifications and protein-mapped identifications, retaining spectrum–peptide identities, all tied first-rank hits in their original order, ranking evidence and all compatible accessions. Each hit in both files must carry its target, decoy or target-and-decoy classification based on those protein mappings. Files: indexed.idXML, search.idXML.
4. final_answer/04_psm_qvalues/
   idXML
   Target leading-hit PSM q-values before the final 1% threshold and the target/decoy evidence supporting them. The supporting target/decoy evidence may be identified in the submitted original search output; it need not be recomputed into an extra table. Files: qvalues.idXML.
5. final_answer/05_psm_accepted/
   idXML
   The thresholded PSM set with acceptance criteria. Files: accepted.idXML.
6. final_answer/06_feature_identification_links/
   featureXML
   Feature-to-identification relationships and unassigned identifications, preserving multiplicity. Files: mapped.featureXML.
7. final_answer/07_isotope_peptides/
   native peptide isotope TSV
   Native peptide-level abundance, incorporation, fit and ambiguity evidence for the incorporation report, excluding peptides explained solely by one natural-abundance component (relative isotope abundance below 5%). Preserve unresolved fields actually reported within the included records. Do not add natural-abundance-only or placeholder peptide rows. For identifications with no incorporation-report entry, retain the submitted identification/feature evidence; do not invent estimates or per-peptide failure reasons. Files: peptides.tsv.
8. final_answer/08_isotope_groups/
   native group isotope TSV
   Complete native group and protein summaries covering every peptide with an accepted isotope-pattern fit and at least one supported relative-isotope-abundance estimate, including peptides with only natural-abundance isotope patterns, with each peptide's unique or shared protein assignments. Files: groups.tsv.

items.title: Small-variant differences among haploid yeast strains
items.summary: Call small variants jointly in four haploid yeast strains, annotate nuclear and mitochondrial effects, and list confident differences between every pair of strains.
items.task_text:
Small-variant differences among haploid yeast strains

Task
Characterize small genomic differences among four haploid S. cerevisiae laboratory strains, preserving complete variant and annotation evidence. The strains are not treatment replicates. Use a haplotype-based Bayesian method for joint small-variant calling, allowing nearby linked changes to inform haploid genotypes. Compare normalized, annotated sample genotypes with explicit confidence filters, not merely presence in independently called variant lists. Distinguish nuclear and mitochondrial coding consequences.

Inputs
- Four strains' eight complete paired-read files and sample/mate identities.
- Ensembl R64-1-1 release-115 reference and annotation, including nuclear and mitochondrial sequences.

Key parameters and conditions
- Align paired Illumina reads using maximal exact-match seeds with affine-gap Smith–Waterman extension; select coordinate-duplicate representatives by summed base qualities. Remove adapter sequence only where the two mates of a pair overlap (insert shorter than the read), without sequence-based adapter detection, and do not merge mates. Retain a pair only when both reads satisfy Q15 qualified bases with at most 40% unqualified bases, at most five ambiguous bases and minimum length 15 nt. Add no fixed-length trimming or sliding-window trimming. First retain alignment records marked as proper pairs, then remove duplicates; do not downsample or add region/depth exclusions.
- Jointly genotype all four haploid samples without a population/HWE prior, with genotype qualities and minimum base/MAPQ 20. A candidate alternate allele must have count≥2 and fraction≥0.20 within at least one single sample; do not pool counts across the four samples to meet these thresholds. Retain all candidate sites (variant probability cutoff 0).
- Normalize against the supplied reference and stop on REF mismatches. Preserve multiallelic and complex records without atomizing or splitting. Retain sample-level missing and low-confidence calls.
- Build an effect-annotation database from the supplied genome and gene annotation. Report all consequences/transcripts in the standard 16-field ANN representation, including HIGH, MODERATE, LOW or MODIFIER impact categories, using the applicable nuclear/yeast-mitochondrial genetic code in each compartment. For every unordered pair, select differing nonmissing haploid genotypes with QUAL≥30 and DP≥10/GQ≥20 in both samples. Absence or missing genotype is not evidence of reference identity. Briefly discuss uncertain calls and comparison limitations.
- Apply upstream/downstream effect-annotation windows of zero bases. Annotate the complete normalized call set; derive pairwise contrasts from its unannotated normalized representation, retaining all four sample columns S01–S04 even in pairwise or empty VCFs. Use lexicographic pair names. Soft-clip supplementary alignments and retain supplementary mapping quality rather than applying its special reduction. Report alignment statistics on the proper-pair BAM.

   JSON
   Complete native paired-read QC/processing report qc.json. Files: {sample}/qc.json.
2. final_answer/02_filtered_reads/{sample}/
   FASTQ
   Both processed mate files. Files: {sample}/forward.fastq.gz, {sample}/reverse.fastq.gz.
3. final_answer/03_aligned/{sample}.bam
   BAM + index
   Coordinate-sorted alignments before proper-pair selection.
4. final_answer/04_proper_pairs/{sample}.bam
   BAM + index
   Proper-pair selected alignments.
5. final_answer/05_deduplicated/{sample}/
   BAM + native text metrics
   deduplicated.bam and duplicates.txt with the coordinate-duplicate library metrics. Files: {sample}/deduplicated.bam, {sample}/duplicates.txt.
6. final_answer/06_alignment_reports/{sample}/
   native text
   stats.txt: complete flag, sequence, quality, insert-size and coverage statistics on the proper-pair BAM. Files: {sample}/stats.txt.
7. final_answer/07_joint_raw.vcf
   VCF
   Complete unfiltered four-sample joint calls, with haploid genotypes, DP/GQ and observed counts for REF and every ALT. Use RO/AO or equivalent allele-ordered AD counts; retain missing values.
8. final_answer/08_joint_normalized.vcf
   VCF
   Complete normalized joint call set preserving record representation.
9. final_answer/09_annotation_resources/
   resource metadata + native annotation database
   Genome/annotation identity, compartment-specific genetic codes and the effect-annotation database built from the supplied resources. Retain the native database and resource metadata.
10. final_answer/10_annotated_nuclear.vcf
   VCF
   Complete nuclear consequences and sample-level genotypes. Include complete standard ANN consequence/transcript records and impact categories.
11. final_answer/11_annotated_mitochondrial.vcf
   VCF
   Complete mitochondrial consequences and sample-level genotypes. Include complete standard ANN consequence/transcript records and impact categories.

   For each nuclear/mitochondrial compartment, a complete native effect-summary HTML and gene-statistics TSV, named nuclear.html, mitochondrial.html, nuclear.genes.tsv and mitochondrial.genes.tsv.

items.title: Multiplex tissue imaging and cell neighborhoods
items.summary: Correct, stitch and register ten imaging cycles, segment nuclei in four tissue cores, assign cell phenotypes and test which phenotypes sit next to each other.
items.task_text:
Multiplex tissue imaging and cellular neighborhoods

Task
Analyze ten multiplex-imaging cycles and four tissue cores to quantify cells, assign phenotypes and characterize within-core neighborhoods. Preserve all supplied channels and cores; these cores are not biological replicates and do not support clinical or between-group claims. Derive nuclear instances and per-cell marker measurements from registered multiplex images. Use marker-intensity mixture modeling with the supplied phenotype rules, retaining uncertain assignments. Test spatial phenotype association against within-core label permutations; cells are spatial observations, not independent biological replicates.

Inputs
- All ten imaging cycles, four-core identity information and channel/cycle metadata.
- The supplied marker and phenotype definitions and image calibration.

Key parameters and conditions
- Estimate illumination by retrospective low-rank plus sparse decomposition into flat-field and dark-field components, solved with the original inexact augmented-Lagrangian scheme on the per-pixel intensity-sorted tile stack with fixed absolute smoothness weights of 0.1 (flat field) and 0.01 (dark field) rather than data-derived weights. Stitch tiles and register imaging cycles jointly using phase-correlation alignments organized by tile adjacency and a spanning tree. Detect TMA cores with a pretrained UNet probability map of the downsampled DNA channel, locating core centers and using active contours for core masks. Use alignment channel 0/max shift 30 and core-detection channel 0/downsampling 5/sensitivity 0.3/buffer 2. Preserve mask-label–CellID linkage, centroid coordinates and all channels; integer mask labels are arbitrary.
- Segment nuclei with a model pretrained on multiplex fluorescence images from diverse tissues, predicting nuclear-center/distance and interior maps followed by deep watershed. Use nuclear channel 0 at 0.65 µm/pixel, center-maxima threshold 0.1 and interior threshold 0.2. Do not expand nuclear masks into whole-cell masks. Measure mean marker intensity and morphological/spatial properties within each labeled nucleus, preserving CellID and centroid coordinates.
- Retain all cells and markers, including DNA channels, with raw intensities and natural-log(1+x) values. For each core use automatic marker gating by a two-component intensity mixture: clip each raw marker at its 0.01st/99.99th percentiles for the gate fit, apply log1p once, fit a two-component Gaussian mixture (seed 0), and use the midpoint of its two means as the gate. Rescale log1p raw marker values to [0,1] with the gate at 0.5, then apply the supplied phenotype rules. Use raw intensities, not already logged X, as the source for gating and rescaling. Do not subsample or replace the rules with manual gates.
- Within each core, build a radius-46 graph in the untransformed generic core-image pixel coordinates, without self-loops or cross-core edges. Compute unweighted row-normalized phenotype interaction and neighborhood enrichment with 1,000 permutations/seed 0. Retain counts and z-scores including undefined values; they are not p-values. Do not rescale coordinates to infer a physical radius.
- Deep-watershed postprocessing uses maxima radius 1 pixel, interior smoothing 2 pixels and minimum object/hole area 15 pixels. Keep unresolved phenotypes as Unknown. Store each image or mask as one TIFF series. Rescale log1p intensity piecewise linearly: [minimum, gate] to [0, 0.5] and [gate, maximum] to [0.5, 1].

Required results
1. final_answer/01_illumination/
   TIFF
   flatfield.tiff and darkfield.tiff for each input cycle, preserving all channels; {cycle} is the input cycle file name. Files: {cycle}/flatfield.tiff, {cycle}/darkfield.tiff.
2. final_answer/02_registered_images/
   OME-TIFF
   registered.ome.tiff: complete registered multichannel image with spatial/channel metadata. Files: registered.ome.tiff.
3. final_answer/03_core_images/{core}/
   OME-TIFF + TIFF
   image.ome.tiff and mask.tiff for each of the four extracted cores, with all channels and extraction masks. {core} numbers the four cores 1–4 in row-major order of their positions in the registered image (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right); use the same numbers in every result. Files: image.ome.tiff, mask.tiff.
4. final_answer/04_nuclear_masks/{core}.tiff
   TIFF labeled mask
   Complete nuclear labels and segmentation diagnostics.
5. final_answer/05_cell_measurements/{core}.csv
   CSV + H5AD
   The measurement CSV and a same-core .h5ad with log1p marker matrix X, raw intensities in raw/X and their identities in raw/var. CSV/H5AD preserve CellID, X_centroid, Y_centroid and every measured marker. Files: {core}.csv, {core}.h5ad.
6. final_answer/06_phenotypes/{core}/
   H5AD
   Phenotypes with complete measurements and identity linkage. Use CellID as observation identity, categorical obs/phenotype and rescaled marker X; retain raw intensities. Files: cells.h5ad.
7. final_answer/07_spatial_graphs/{core}/
   H5AD
   Within-core connectivity and coordinate/identity metadata. Store obsm/spatial and obsp/spatial_connectivities, obsp/spatial_distances. Files: cells.h5ad.
8. final_answer/08_interactions/{core}/
   H5AD
   Unweighted row-normalized phenotype interactions. Store the phenotype-labelled matrix in uns/phenotype_interactions, ordered by obs/phenotype categories. Files: cells.h5ad.
9. final_answer/09_neighborhood_enrichment/{core}/
   H5AD
   Complete enrichment counts and z-scores with phenotype labels and undefined entries. Store count and zscore matrices in uns/phenotype_nhood_enrichment, ordered by obs/phenotype categories. Files: cells.h5ad.

items.title: LC-MS features and ion relationships
items.summary: Detect and align chromatographic peaks across all LC-MS runs, fill in missing peaks from the raw signal, and annotate isotopes and co-eluting ions.
items.task_text:
liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry feature quantification and ion relationships

Task
Analyze every supplied liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry acquisition to produce a peak-area matrix and ion-feature annotations, accounting for retention-time drift and missing detections. Compound identification and biological differential-abundance testing are outside scope. Detect chromatographic peaks by continuous-wavelet analysis of accurate-mass regions of interest built from successive centroid scans. Use shared peak landmarks for nonlinear retention-time correction and establish correspondence on corrected times. Recover missing peak areas by integrating the underlying signal, and assess coelution/isotope relationships without claiming confirmed metabolite identities.

Inputs
- All supplied liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry acquisitions and sample identities.
- Class metadata including blanks, batches and distinct pooled-QC preparations; do not combine these classes.

Key parameters and conditions
- For wavelet peak detection, use mass tolerance 3 ppm, peak widths 5–20 s and S/N≥10. Require at least three mass-trace centroids with intensity≥5,000 and apply an intensity-noise threshold of 1,000. Use intensity-weighted mean m/z, wavelet-derived integration limits and minimum overlapping-peak m/z difference −0.001 Da. Recover missing peak areas by integrating raw signal within the established feature bounds, not by rerunning another peak detector or imputing values.
- Use density-based correspondence with RT bandwidth 5 s and m/z bin width 0.01 Da. Before missing-peak integration, require detection in at least 90% of acquisitions in at least one supplied class (minimum sample count 1). Apply the same rule before and after RT correction; do not pool or drop classes.
- For RT landmarks, require peak groups present in at least 70% of all acquisitions and no more than one peak beyond the total number of acquisitions. Fit LOESS correction with span 0.2 and Gaussian-family fitting. Quantify integrated areas in every acquisition; fill missing peaks from the raw signal with no extra m/z or RT window expansion, not with zero or a sample mean.
- For coelution/isotope annotation, group around abundant peaks using a retention-time window whose total width is 0.6 times the estimated FWHM (±0.3×FWHM). Estimate FWHM as 2.35 times the peak’s full time span divided by 6. Use mass tolerances 5 ppm and 0.015 Da, maximum charge 2 and at most 4 expected isotopes. Require the isotope-abundance rule in at least 50% of samples. These annotations are not confirmed compound identities.
- Preserve sample/feature identities, original and corrected times, units and coordinate conventions, and distinguish directly detected peaks from newly integrated peaks. Arbitrary feature/group names do not change scientific credit; plots are optional.
- Use integrated areas (into). An undetected or still-unfillable feature/acquisition cell is NA, not zero. The supplied class labels define the eight grouping classes; do not substitute batch. Missing-peak integration uses the medians of the group members’ m/z and RT bounds, with no extra expansion. Coelution annotation uses only the FWHM grouping and isotope steps, without correlation-based regrouping or adduct inference.

3. final_answer/03_initial_groups/
   TSV
   features.tsv: feature_id, mz, rt, mzmin, mzmax, rtmin, rtmax, npeaks; membership.tsv: feature_id, peak_id; peaks.tsv: peak_id, acquisition, mz, rt, mzmin, mzmax, rtmin, rtmax, into, is_filled; intensities.tsv: feature_id, mz, rt, then one column per acquisition. Feature/peak identifiers must link the files; mz is in Da, rt in seconds. Files: features.tsv, intensities.tsv, membership.tsv, peaks.tsv.
4. final_answer/04_retention_time_correction/
